tasks.title: Embed the five JSON Schemas and add `vloop schema list|show|validate`
tasks.goal: The schemas are the contract every other file in the loop is judged against: Go validates against them now, and the B4 skills will cite them. Every later task's plan fixtures are validated by `state/v1`, so its field list is load-bearing. The schema files are the authority — a Go struct may mirror one but must never be the only definition or accept what the schema rejects.

references.why: 'Schemas' in the Behaviour contract: the five names, every field and enum of each, the snake_case and unknown-keys rules, and the list/show/validate output and error formats
Section 2 fixes where the schemas live: a root `schemas/` directory embedded by the root `embed.go` alongside `all:plugin`
Section 4's proposal fields and their types (`files` an array, `verified` a string) that proposal/v1 formalises
The verdict.json fields (`criteria` entries with criterion/met/evidence, PASS|FAIL) that verdict/v1 formalises
'Metrics and defects': gate_dispute and the finding kinds; metrics-snapshot and defect-record schemas are B3's and must not appear here

acceptance: Five schema documents live in the root `schemas/` directory as `state.v1.json`, `proposal.v1.json`, `verdict.v1.json`, `session.v1.json` and `iteration.v1.json`, each declaring `$schema` https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema; no other schema (metrics snapshot, defect record) is added.

The schemas are embedded by the root `embed.go` (package vloop) and read at runtime only from the embedded FS; a violation is any os.ReadFile/os.Open of a schema path, or a schema whose only definition is a Go struct.
Validation uses github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 — the only new module — against the embedded documents, with no remote `$ref` loading and no network; the binary builds with CGO_ENABLED=0.

Every schema requires a `schema` property whose value must equal the schema's own name (e.g. `state/v1`), uses snake_case keys, and allows unknown keys at every level (no `additionalProperties: false` or `unevaluatedProperties: false`).

state/v1 requires schema, run_id, brief, base, branch, status (planning|running|complete|blocked|stalled|halted), iteration (integer), created, updated, shell (sh|bash|pwsh|powershell|cmd) and tasks; its top-level `properties` are declared in that order.

A state/v1 task requires id (pattern `^T[0-9]+$`), title, goal, kind (feature|fix|refactor|test|docs|chore), files, references (items require path and why, both strings), depends_on, acceptance (minItems 1), verify (minLength 1), status (pending|done|blocked), attempts (integer) and notes; area is an optional string; model and effort are optional objects with optional `work` and `review` keys (model values non-empty strings, effort values low|medium|high|xhigh|max); gate_history is an optional array of {verify, replaced_at, reason, by} with by operator|planner. Task properties are declared in that order.
proposal/v1 requires schema, task, outcome (done|blocked), summary, files (array of strings), verified (string) and notes, with optional gate_dispute requiring reason and evidence.
verdict/v1 requires schema, task, verdict (PASS|FAIL), criteria (items require criterion, met boolean, evidence), findings (items require summary and kind bug|spec-gap|gate-gap) and notes.

session/v1 requires schema, run_id, iteration, phase (plan|work|review), model, effort (a string or null), models_used (an object keyed by model id, each value {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cost_usd} — the snake_case of Claude's modelUsage), started, duration_ms (integer), cost_usd (number), turns (integer), is_error (boolean) and permission_denials (array); task is required for work and review and absent for plan.
iteration/v1 requires schema, run_id, iteration, task, attempt, outcome (done|gate_failed|rejected|blocked|session_error), gate (an object {exit, duration_ms} or null), started and ended.
`vloop schema list` prints the five names sorted, one per line; `--json` prints them as one JSON array. `vloop schema show <name>` prints the schema document.

`vloop schema validate <name> <file>` prints `<file>: ok` and exits 0, or one line per violation as `<file>: <json pointer>: <message>` (the validator's message, the exact instance pointer) and exits 1; `--json` prints `{"ok":bool,"errors":[{"pointer","message"}]}` on both exits. A file that is not JSON is exactly one violation at pointer `""`. `<file>` is printed as the argument was given.
An unknown schema name, for show or validate, prints `vloop: unknown schema "<name>"` on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 2.

Committed tests: internal/schema has, for every schema, at least one fixture under internal/schema/testdata/ that validates and one that fails at a named pointer, exercised by a test; internal/cli has TestSchema* tests covering list, show, validate and the unknown-name error.
No product code or test reads or writes this repo's `.loop/` or `.claude/`, or the home directory; tests work in `t.TempDir()` scratch repos.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, `go mod tidy -diff` prints nothing, and the module builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 for linux and windows and for the host.

tasks.title: Load and save `.vloop/state/state.json`, and add `vloop status` (text, --json, --markdown)
tasks.goal: Every `task` command reads and writes the plan through this layer, so its guarantees — atomic writes, a byte-for-byte stable format, a clear error when the plan is missing, reads that survive a plan failing its schema — are what the rest of the run builds on. `vloop status` is the first reader and proves the loader. Nothing in this slice writes plan.md; `--markdown` prints to stdout.

references.why: 'The plan file' (location, missing-plan and invalid-plan behaviour, atomic and byte-stable writes) and '`vloop status`' (line format, alignment, attempts suffix, --json keys, --markdown content)
the markdown `status --markdown` must carry: header, progress checklist with attempt(s)/blocked notes, and per task its status line, dependencies, files, goal, acceptance and notes, in that wording
the conventions this extends: --json prints one document on stdout on exit 0 and 1, errors are one `vloop: ` stderr line, the repo root is resolved as `config.Root` does
Section 2 names `internal/state/` as the package for state.json load/validate/render

acceptance: Package internal/state loads `.vloop/state/state.json` under the repo root (resolved as B1 does, so commands work from a subdirectory) and validates it against the embedded state/v1 schema; the schema, not a Go struct, decides validity.
A missing plan is `vloop: no plan: .vloop/state/state.json` on stderr, exit 1, nothing on stdout; with --json, stdout still carries one JSON document.
A plan that fails its schema but parses is still readable: `vloop status` prints its normal output and exits 0.

Saving writes a temporary file in `.vloop/state/` and renames it over state.json (no temp file is left behind); the output is 2-space-indented JSON, keys in schema order (top level and task), a trailing newline, and `<`, `>` and `&` written literally rather than as \u003c-style escapes, so loading and saving an unchanged plan written in that format is byte-for-byte identical. Every save sets `updated` to the current time in RFC 3339 UTC.

`vloop status` prints `<run_id> — <status> · <done>/<total> done · <blocked> blocked · iteration <n>` then one line per task `  <id>  <status>  <area>/<kind>  <title>`, each column left-aligned on its widest value with two spaces between, `  (<n> attempt)`/`  (<n> attempts)` appended only when attempts > 0, and `-/<kind>` for a task without area; no trailing spaces.

`vloop status --json` prints `{"run_id","status","iteration","done","total","blocked","tasks":[{"id","status","area","kind","title","attempts"}]}` with keys in that order; a task without area has area null.

`vloop status --markdown` prints to stdout the content render-plan.sh renders — `# Plan — <run_id>`, `## Progress` with `- [x] **T1** — <title>` lines (` · <n> attempt(s)` or ` · **blocked**` appended as render-plan does), `## Tasks` with `### <id> — <title>`, the `` `<status>`<note> · depends on: <ids or none> `` line, `**Files:**`, the goal, `**Acceptance**` bullets, and `**From the last attempt:** <notes>` when notes are set; it writes no file.
status never modifies the plan or writes any file.

Committed tests: internal/state has a test that a plan fixture round-trips byte-for-byte and one that a save leaves no temp file; internal/cli has TestStatus* tests covering text, --json, --markdown and the missing plan.
No product code or test reads or writes this repo's `.loop/` or `.claude/`, or the home directory; tests work in `t.TempDir()` scratch repos.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, `go mod tidy -diff` prints nothing, and the module builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 for linux and windows and for the host.

tasks.title: Add the `shell` and `areas` config keys, and `vloop task list|show` with model/effort resolution
tasks.goal: `areas` is what `task validate` and `task set` check a task's area against, and `shell` is what the B4/B5 planner records in the plan; both must exist before those tasks. `task show --json` is the API the B4 skills will call instead of parsing state.json, so it must carry the whole task plus the model and effort each of its sessions would resolve to, and where each value came from.

references.why: 'New config keys: shell and areas', the `task list`/`task show` rows and the Resolution rule, and the Constraints paragraph on the one allowed change to B1's tests
the config key table, sources (default/file/env), `config list|get|set` output formats, the `vloop: invalid value "<v>" for <key>: want …` message, and effort's unset rendering
the shell decision (default sh on macOS/Linux, pwsh on Windows; the plan's shell governs its gates) and the fixed `kind` list

acceptance: config.Keys gains `shell` then `areas`, after effort.review. `shell` accepts sh|bash|pwsh|powershell|cmd (the invalid-value message lists them in that order) and defaults to sh on darwin and linux and pwsh on windows; VLOOP_SHELL overrides it.

`areas` defaults to an empty list; `config set areas cli,brief,config` stores a TOML array in .vloop/config.toml; `config get areas` and `config list` print it comma-joined (`areas=cli,brief,config (file)`, `areas= (default)` when empty); --json gives an array (`[]` when empty). Each entry must match lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, otherwise exit 2 with B1's invalid-value message and the file untouched; `''` removes the key.

The only changes to B1's tests are the pinned `config list` expectations in cmd/vloop/e2e_test.go and internal/cli/config_test.go, extended with the shell and areas lines (and their --json entries); no other assertion in those files is changed, loosened or removed.
`vloop task list` prints exactly the task lines of `vloop status` (no header); --json prints the same array `status --json` carries in `tasks`.

`vloop task show <id>` prints the whole task and two resolution lines, exactly `model   work <m> (<source>) · review <m> (<source>)` and `effort  work <e> (<source>) · review <e> (<source>)`, with `-` for an unset effort; source is task, env, file or default.
Resolution for session kind k (work, review): the task's model.k, else VLOOP_MODEL_<K>, else model.k in the config file, else the default; the same for effort with VLOOP_EFFORT_<K> and effort.k.
`vloop task show <id> --json` prints the task object with every field it has in the plan, plus `resolved: {work: {model, model_source, effort, effort_source}, review: {…}}`, effort null when unset.
An unknown task id is `vloop: no task <id>` on stderr, exit 1; a missing plan is the T2 no-plan error.

tasks.title: Add `vloop task validate` with every structural rule
tasks.goal: Every write command refuses to produce a plan that fails this check, so it is the definition of a sound plan for the rest of the slice. It ports every fatal rule of the shell loop's `.loop/amend.sh check` and adds the new fields; the driver's plan-time gate-shape rejections are B5's and do not belong here.

references.why: '`vloop task validate`': the exact problem and warning lines, the closing `plan ok` / `<n> problem(s)` line, exit codes, and the cycle-start rule
check(): the fatal rules being ported (no verify, no acceptance, dangling dependency, duplicate id, cycle); its advisories (shared gate files, passing gates, HEAD diffs) are out of scope

acceptance: Output is one line per finding, `✗` for a problem and `!` for a warning, then `plan ok` when there are no problems or `<n> problem(s)` (literally, e.g. `2 problem(s)`) when there are; exit 1 on any problem, else 0. validate never writes.

Problems, with exactly this wording: `✗ schema: <pointer>: <message>` per schema violation (this is how an empty verify or empty acceptance is reported); `✗ duplicate task id: <id>`; `✗ <id> depends on <dep>, which does not exist`; `✗ depends_on cycle: <a> -> <b> -> <a>`; `✗ <id>: reference does not resolve: <path>`; `✗ <id>: reference has no reason: <path>`; `✗ <id>: area "<a>" is not in areas (<comma-space list>)`; `✗ <id>: no area — areas is set`.
A cycle is reported as the loop itself (not the path into it), starting from its lowest task id by the number after T; a reference path resolves relative to the repo root and may name a directory.
The area rules apply only when `areas` is set in config; with `areas` empty an area is optional and unchecked.
Warning (exit stays 0): `! <id>: no gate_history reason` for each gate_history entry with an empty reason.
A missing plan is the no-plan error; --json prints one JSON document on stdout on exit 0 and 1.
Every rule has a committed fixture that passes and one where it fires, under internal/state/testdata/validate/, exercised by tests; internal/cli has TestTaskValidate* tests.
No product code or test reads or writes this repo's `.loop/` or `.claude/`, or the home directory; tests work in `t.TempDir()` scratch repos.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, `go mod tidy -diff` prints nothing, and the module builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 for linux and windows and for the host.

tasks.goal: These let the operator amend a plan without hand-editing JSON. They are the first write commands, so they prove the save path end to end: only state.json changes, atomically, in the stable format, and nothing is written when the plan is already invalid or the result would be.

references.why: the `task reset|note|drop|set` rows and the rules under them: drop's dependent refusal, set's fields, validation messages and `''` clearing, the no-task and invalid-plan errors
the shell loop's reset/note/drop semantics being ported, including drop refusing a depended-on task

acceptance: `task reset <id>` sets status pending and attempts 0; `task note <id> '<text>'` replaces notes; `task drop <id>` removes the task, refusing with `vloop: <dependent> depends on <id>`, exit 1, when another task depends on it.

tasks.title: Add `vloop task verify` with gate_history, and `vloop task gate` in the plan's shell
tasks.goal: B3 reclassifies the failures a wrong gate caused, which is only possible if every gate replacement is recorded with who, when, why and the old command — so `task verify` requires a reason and appends to gate_history. `task gate` runs one gate as the driver will, in the plan's own shell rather than the config's, so a plan written for sh says so on a machine without sh.

references.why: the `task gate` and `task verify` rules: per-shell invocation, output and --json forms, the missing-shell message, --reason, the unchanged-command refusal
'A gate can be the defect': what gate_history records and why; this slice stores the facts and computes nothing from them

acceptance: `task gate <id>` runs the task's verify from the repo root in the plan's `shell` (not config's): sh/bash as `<shell> -c <cmd>`, pwsh/powershell as `<shell> -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command <cmd>`, cmd as `cmd /C <cmd>`; the gate's output is streamed, then `gate <id>: pass (<duration>)` exits 0 or `gate <id>: fail (exit <n>, <duration>)` exits 1, n being the verify's own exit code.
`task gate <id> --json` prints only `{"task","passed","exit","duration_ms"}` (in that order) on stdout, the gate's own output going to stderr.
When the plan's shell is not on PATH: `vloop: this plan's gates are <shell> commands and <shell> is not on PATH`, exit 1. task gate writes nothing.

`task verify <id> '<cmd>' --reason '<text>'` appends `{verify: <old command>, replaced_at: <RFC 3339 UTC>, reason, by: "operator"}` to the task's gate_history and sets the new command; nothing else changes except `updated`.

Without --reason: `vloop: required flag(s) "reason" not set`, exit 2. Setting the command the task already has: `vloop: <id> already has that verify command`, exit 1. Neither, nor an empty command, nor an invalid plan, writes anything.
Tests of `task gate` use sh where it exists and skip the other shells when absent, saying so (t.Skip with the reason); a test may use a PATH test double for a shell.
